raw_response:
I have been growing cotton on this land for decades. Quzhou soil I know well — it holds water if I don't overdo irrigation, and it responds to potassium, which is good for fiber length. At 70, I can still manage 5 mu myself with my family helping at picking time. I will not change what works.

Cotton goes in after the last frost, around Grain Rain — late April. I deep-plough before planting. I have done rotary tillage before but I find deep ploughing breaks up the compaction layer and the roots go deeper, which matters when summer gets hot and dry. I depend on my well — I will irrigate before planting to ensure good germination, then again at seedling stage, flowering, and boll formation. Four times is enough if the rains cooperate. If it is a dry year I add one more.

For seed I use hybrid. I switched years ago. The yield is better and the plants are more uniform. My old neighbors who kept traditional varieties fall behind at market.

Fertilizer: I apply base fertilizer before planting — phosphorus and potassium go in with the plough. Nitrogen I split — part as base, part as topdress when bolls are setting. That is when the plant needs it most and I do not want to push too much vegetative growth early.

Pesticides — cotton here always has bollworm and aphids. I watch carefully and spray when I actually see pressure, not on a fixed schedule. Usually six times gets through the season, sometimes fewer if I catch things early with the right timing.

I expect around 290 kg of seed cotton per mu. Some years I get more, some years drought or storms cut it. That is farming.
